title: Herd helper CLI (deterministic spawn/wait/collect)
description: Layer 2. Deterministic helper wrapping the herdr socket API so the wave loop is a handful of calls: spawn <tick> (worktree + agent start + prompt from tick body + runners.toml routing), wait-wave (event-driven fan-in via events.subscribe/events.wait on pane.agent_status_changed - no polling), collect <tick> (branch has commits + RESULT.md, .tick/ boundary check), cleanup --preview, reconcile (rebuild run state after orchestrator death from tracker + herdr snapshot + agent_session IDs). Open decisions at flesh-out: standalone tkherd vs tk herd subcommand (Go, alongside tk); socket protocol client vs shelling to herdr CLI. Rough deliverables: the CLI, socket event client, run-state manifest format, integration tests against a named herdr test session, herdr-runner.md updated to prefer the helper.
notes: 2026-08-11 14:06 - Branch strategy: epic/gyz stacked on epic/ias (PR #37 pending merge to main). When #37 merges, epic/gyz PR diff against main collapses to layer-2 work only. Base branch recorded as main.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator wave loop expressible in <=5 helper calls per wave; fan-in proven event-driven (no polling loops); kill -9 of the orchestrator mid-wave followed by reconcile recovers the run without losing worker output; cleanup --preview shows exactly what apply then removes; works from at least two orchestrator harnesses.
